Grace / Marissa — quick internal note before we lock anything with the customer.

- Australia/Sydney flips off DST on Sun 4 Apr at 03:00 local; clocks go back one hour. That means if we schedule for Tue 6 Apr 09:00 Australia/Sydney explicit timezone, attendees should see the correct time, but people with non-Sydney zones (e.g., Lord Howe or some NZ zones) could see differences.
- Recommendation: add the invite in Australia/Sydney TZ and include explicit start times in UTC and in ET/CET in the body. Also mark the calendar description: “Times listed in Australia/Sydney; double-check local offset.”
- For minimal confusion, propose both 08:30 AEST and 09:30 AEST options and ask them to confirm. If they accept both, we can auto-accept the earlier one and invite the EU stakeholders with a clear note.

I'll prepare a short note we can paste into the invite. Also suggest we record and send a recap in case someone arrives at the wrong local time.

—Ben
